children: Most Gulf equity markets edged higher in early trade on Wednesday, buoyed by restored crude flows from a key Saudi pipeline and growing optimism over a diplomatic resolution to the US-Iran conflict.

Saudi Arabia has resumed operations on its East-West Pipeline and could restart crude exports from the Red Sea port of Yanbu as early as Tuesday, three sources briefed on the matter said, in a sign of broader recovery in Middle East supply.
Despite US President Donald Trump alternating between stark threats and hints of an imminent accord in response to Iranian defiance, diplomatic efforts at the United Nations continued to gain ground.

This momentum toward de-escalation, coupled with recovering regional supply, alleviated market strain and dragged benchmark Brent crude below the $100-a-barrel mark for the first time since September 8.
